name: Meningeal Thermoelectric Pressure Lance
description:
The MTPL-2 exploits thermoelectric induction to generate rapid, localized heating within the meningeal membranes surrounding the brain. A directional microwave-band emitter penetrates the skull and preferentially excites the fluid-dense dural and arachnoid layers, producing a steep thermal gradient. The resulting expansion of cerebrospinal fluid within the enclosed cranial vault creates acute intracranial pressure spikes, manifesting in the target as sudden incapacitating headache, nausea, loss of motor coordination, and at sustained exposure, hemorrhagic stroke.

The weapon's distinctive characteristic is its graduated effect curve. At low power settings, the MTPL-2 produces a debilitating but non-lethal pressure event lasting several minutes — useful for crowd control or capture operations. At maximum output, sustained for more than three seconds, the cranial pressure becomes unsurvivable without immediate decompression surgery. Operators describe the kill as 'clean from the outside,' with no external wound and internal damage consistent with spontaneous aneurysm.

Arcturus Defense Solutions developed the Crown as a successor to older microwave crowd-dispersal systems, arguing that precision targeting eliminated the indiscriminate harm of area-effect predecessors. The lance form factor allows engagement up to forty meters with a focused beam, making it effective for both individual neutralization and controlled area denial when swept across a crowd. Its use in the GLMZ Port Authority Suppression of 2181 — where seventeen dock workers died of 'simultaneous cerebrovascular events' — remains officially uninvestigated.
specifications:
effective range: 2–40 meters
beam width: Adjustable, 0.3° to 12° arc
power settings: 3 (Suppress / Incapacitate / Lethal)
lethal threshold: 3.1 seconds sustained at max output
power source: Dedicated 18V thermal cell, 8 sustained seconds at max
weight: 3.1 kg with cell
cooling: Passive ceramic radiator fins along barrel
tactical_use: Used by state-contracted security forces for both crowd suppression and targeted assassination with plausible medical deniability. At Suppress setting, operators sweep the beam across gatherings to disperse without direct confrontation. In single-target mode, the Crown is walked up the torso toward the head, maximizing disorientation before the lethal threshold is reached. Military doctrine recommends two-operator teams — one targeting, one providing cover during the extended engagement window.
cultural_context: Among protest organizers and labor agitators in GLMZ, the Crown has become a symbol of state violence that cannot be seen or proven. The phrase 'died of a headache' is used bitterly in activist communities to describe colleagues killed at demonstrations. Arcturus Defense Solutions has successfully lobbied for classification of MTPL-2 casualty data as proprietary security information. Possession of the weapon by non-state actors is exceptionally rare and treated by law enforcement as a maximum-priority threat.
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions contracted riot units
Cassius Verne, a disgraced ADS field tester operating independently
story_hooks: A journalist investigating the Port Authority Suppression of 2181 has obtained internal communications referencing the MTPL-2 — she needs someone to keep her alive long enough to publish.
A stolen Crown surfaces in the Outerring black market; every faction in the city wants it, and the original theft may have been an inside job.
A character with a neural implant discovers their hardware is partially shielding them from the weapon's effect — Arcturus Defense Solutions dispatches a team to quietly recover them for study.
A political candidate drops dead on stage from apparent stroke; the players are hired by a rival campaign to prove it wasn't natural — then hired by someone else to make sure they don't.
